context.title: Count the requests the fleet gateway has open to each model
context.body:
### Description of your changes

Towards #476.

Nothing in the `modelplane_*` surface showed what callers are waiting on. When callers disconnect and the engine isn't told, it keeps decoding. On one deployment the engine held 29 requests while the gateway had 2 open, and new requests queued behind output nobody read. Both engine gauges were there, and nothing showed the gap. The direction is in https://github.com/modelplaneai/modelplane/issues/476#issuecomment-6305724060.

Envoy counts the requests it has open upstream in `envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_active`, per cluster it builds, and the collector already scraped it from every gateway pod and dropped it. It's now `modelplane_frontend_requests_active`, kept only where it counts what callers are waiting on:

- On the fleet's `inference-gateway`. Each inference cluster's `cluster-gateway` counts the same requests again, so its copy is dropped, and a sum counts each request once.
- For the cluster of a `ModelService`'s route. Envoy's own clusters, and routes such as Grafana's and the OTLP receiver's, are dropped.

Envoy names that cluster `httproute/<namespace>/<service>/rule/0`, after compose-model-route's AIGatewayRoute. The series carries `namespace`, the same label an engine's series carry, and `service`. The work is done by `metric_relabel_configs` on the gateway job, at scrape time, because both drops are on labels a `MetricMapping` can't select on.

Envoy's count drops when a caller leaves, as the 2 against 29 shows. So comparing it with an engine's running and waiting requests catches the case this is for. The telemetry docs show the query.

Run through the collector with a real `/stats/prometheus` from an Envoy Gateway v1.8.4 fleet gateway, the version Modelplane pins, served once as the fleet gateway and once as a cluster gateway. Only the fleet gateway's three model routes came out, each with `namespace` and `service` and no Envoy labels.

I have: <!-- You MUST either [x] check or [ ] ~strike through~ every item. -->

- [x] Read and followed Modelplane's [contribution process](https://github.com/modelplaneai/modelplane/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Run `nix flake check` (or `./nix.sh flake check`) and made sure it passes.
- [x] Added or updated tests covering any composition function changes.
- [x] Signed off every commit with `git commit -s`.

commits.messageBody:
Nothing in the modelplane_* surface showed what callers were waiting on.
An engine whose callers disconnected without it being told kept
decoding: on one deployment the engine held 29 requests while the
gateway had 2 open, and new requests queued behind output nobody read.
Both engine gauges were there; nothing showed the gap.

Envoy counts the requests it has open upstream in
envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_active, per cluster it built, and the
collector already scraped it from every gateway and dropped it. It's
now modelplane_frontend_requests_active, kept only where it means what
callers are waiting on: on the fleet's inference-gateway, not each
inference cluster's cluster-gateway, which counts the same requests
again, and only for the cluster of a ModelService's route, not Envoy's
own clusters or routes such as Grafana's. Envoy names that cluster
httproute/<namespace>/<service>/rule/0, so the series carries namespace,
the same one an engine's series carry, and service. Relabeling at
scrape time does this, because both drops are on labels a
MetricMapping can't select on.

The telemetry docs show how to compare it with an engine's running and
waiting requests. Envoy's count drops when a caller leaves, which the
2 against 29 shows, so the comparison catches the case it's for.

Towards #476.
